thread.title: Apple To Ship Revamped iPad Pro in June Q, Says Rosenblatt

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Apple To Ship Revamped iPad Pro in June Q, Says Rosenblatt
text:
Mock-up of what a revamped Apple iPad Pro might look like, created by Ben Geskin, @VenyaGeskin1. Apple ’s ( AAPL ) prepping to release a revamped “ iPad Pro ” with a slimmer bezel and no home button and the “ Face ID ” function in the June-ending quarter, according to a note this morning from Rosenblatt analyst Jun Zhang ,
Zhang, who has a Buy rating on Apple shares, and a $180 price target, thinks the new devices can offset some weakness that he thinks is persisting with sales of the iPhone X.
He’s modeling “total iPad production to be between 16-18 million units, with 6-8 million iPad Pro models likely implementing 3D sensing functionality in the June quarter."
"Our research suggests the new iPad should be ready for mass production with a release date likely in late-Q2."
A revamped iPad Pro has been hypothesized for a number of months, with Bloomberg ’s Mark Gurman and Alex Webb writing about the matter back in November . A fellow named Ben Geskin did a nice mockup back at the time of what it might look like.
Zhang also thinks the same quarter may see a smaller version of Apple’s “HomePod” smart speaker, though he doesn’t offer a time frame for such a device.
"Apple’s HomePod sales are on track to meet Apple’s 5 million unit target,” he writes. "If released, we believe a lower-end HomePod mod- el could help Apple further penetrate the low-end smart speaker market possi- bly later this year."
A smaller, cheaper model has also been speculated since the device went on sale last month.
All of these prospects offset what Zhang postulates are iPhone X sales that continue to disappoint, citing sales during China’s New Year celebrations. The device “did not sell well during the Chinese New Year,” he writes, adding “we are not surprised with the quick cooldown of iPhone X sales following Chinese New Year."
"It is our view many consumers are awaiting an expected 6.1-inch LCD iPhone—a larger screen iPhone at a lower retail price."
Zhang cuts his estimate for iPhone sales for the March quarter to 50 million from 52 million. He’s holding onto an estimate for June of 38 million units, as he thinks the introduction of a version of the iPhone X in a red finish may offset the weak sales at the moment.
Apple shares are down $1.41, or 0.8%, at $175.26.
